title: The box task - a method for assessing in-vehicle system demand
author: Trommler, Morgenstern, et al.

steps.title: Assemble experimental hardware
steps.instruction: Set up a computer with a monitor, a steering wheel equipped with a button, a gas pedal, and a vibration module that can be mounted on the participant’s shoulders.

steps.title: Configure Box Task software
steps.instruction: Load the Box Task (BT) program so that a displayed box changes its lateral position (simulating lane maintenance) and its size (simulating headway) continuously in a sinusoidal pattern; display inner and outer guide boxes that define the acceptable boundaries.

steps.title: Configure tactile DRT
steps.instruction: Activate the tactile Detection‑Response Task (DRT) module to deliver a vibration signal on the participant’s shoulders at random intervals of three to five seconds; program the steering‑wheel button as the response key.

steps.title: Prepare participant instructions
steps.instruction: Provide written instructions that explain the primary task (Box Task) and the secondary tasks; inform participants that the Box Task is the primary task and they must “drive” as safely as possible while also performing any secondary task.

steps.title: Practice BT+DRT
steps.instruction: Allow each participant to practice the combined Box Task and tactile DRT until they feel comfortable operating the steering wheel, gas pedal, and responding to the vibration signal.

steps.title: Run baseline trial
steps.instruction: Conduct a baseline run in which the participant performs the Box Task and tactile DRT together without any secondary task, recording all data.

steps.title: Execute dual‑task trial
steps.instruction: For each secondary‑task condition, run a trial as follows:

substeps.instruction: a. Start the trial and give the participant 30 seconds to become familiar with the Box Task only.
b. After the 30‑second familiarisation, present an exclamation‑mark visual cue and a beep sound to signal the start of the secondary task.
c. Throughout the trial, continue to present the tactile DRT vibration at random 3–5 second intervals; the participant must press the steering‑wheel button in response.

d. Keep the trial running for a total duration of 210 seconds, during which the participant must keep the box within the inner and outer boundaries using the steering wheel (lateral control) and gas pedal (size control).

steps.title: Repeat for all conditions
steps.instruction: Repeat the dual‑task trial procedure for every secondary‑task condition used in the study.

steps.title: Log trial data
steps.instruction: For each trial, generate a logging file that includes a header with the experiment time and participant ID, and for every recorded frame store:

substeps.instruction: Angle wheel (lateral change of the steering wheel)
Angle pedal (deflection of the gas pedal)
Position of the box in pixels
Size of the box in pixels

steps.title: Analyze Box Task performance
steps.instruction: Using the logged data (e.g., in Matlab), calculate the following measures:

substeps.instruction: Number of lateral error states (box exceeds outer boundary while size is within limits)
Number of longitudinal error states (box size exceeds inner or outer boundary)
Duration of each lateral and longitudinal error state
Mean lateral position (average deviation to left or right)
Mean longitudinal size (average deviation from ideal size)

steps.title: Analyze DRT performance
steps.instruction: Determine DRT performance by calculating the hit rate (percentage of correct button presses) and the mean reaction time for correct responses.
